import pandas as pd

# Load the time_series_data.csv dataset
df_time_series = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')

# Extract the 'CE' and 'Depot' columns
ce_values = df_time_series['CE'].values
depot_values = df_time_series['Depot'].values

# Identify the index of the maximum 'Depot' value
max_index = depot_values.argmax()

# Determine the corresponding 'CE' value
peak_ce = ce_values[max_index]

# Convert the 'CE' value to a century
peak_century = (peak_ce // 100) * 100

peak_century

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the time_series_data.csv dataset
df_time_series = pd.read_csv('/data/time_series_data.csv')

# Plot the 'CE' and 'Depot_inter' columns to visualize the trend
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(df_time_series['CE'], df_time_series['Depot_inter'], label='Depot Interpolated')
plt.xlabel('CE (Common Era)')
plt.ylabel('Depot Interpolated Z Values')
plt.title('Depot Interpolated Z Values Over Time')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)
plt.show()
